articles.name: Release notes through 2026-07-24
articles.title: Release notes through 2026-07-24
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of what was released last month.

This week's release notes include:

  • Admin Center
  • Voice
  • Contact Center
  • Apps and integrations
  • Mobile SDK's
  • App Marketplace
  • Products with no updates this week

Admin Center

New:

  • Admins on Enterprise plans will see a new permission option called "Manage Zendesk Support apps" when creating or editing custom roles. This permission appears under the Channels section of the custom role configuration page.
  • Admin Center now shows proactive reminders 5 minutes and 1 minute before your session reaches its maximum duration and you're signed out. Once signed out, the sign-in page will display that it was due to the maximum duration being met. 

Fixed:

  • Notifications for API tokens that will be automatically deactivated or deleted starting July 28 were sent on July 23, and again on July 27. 

Voice

New:

  • Released the ability to auto-accept calls on PSTN lines. Rollout started on July 20 and will end on July 29.

Fixed:

  • The Voice API in Messaging was updated and is now compatible with the Help Center authentication. Before, if the option "Turn on help center authentication" was enabled, the messaging widget would throw a 422 error when using Voice. Following the deployment, we also fixed a CORS issue where the authentication would fail if the widget was hosted on an external (non-Zendesk) domain. 
  • Fixed a bug where the agent ringtone configuration appeared in other agents' profiles, falsely implying one agent could change another's ringtone. In reality, agents can only modify their own ringtone. 
  • Fixed a bug in which the custom ringtone would continue to ring if the agent changed their status while the call was ringing. 

Contact Center

New:

  • When using the channel switcher to place an outbound call from a ticket, if you use the “Enter phone number” option, the call will be linked to the ticket. The agent can clear the linkage if needed.
  • Agents are now able to download logs to troubleshoot issues, with visibility into agent activity, state changes, API calls, warnings, and errors.
  • Agents can now turn on browser notifications for voice calls to stay aware of incoming calls even when the browser is not in focus. When enabled, notifications show caller information, and clicking them takes agents to the Zendesk tab, where they can accept or reject the call.
  • Added support for Jabra headset controls, allowing users to answer, mute, unmute, and end calls directly from supported headset buttons while keeping call and availability states in sync with Agent Workspace. 
  • Admins can now enable automatic call acceptance for agents, set on a per-user basis.
  • Supervisor monitor & barge - This new feature provides supervisors with two new ways to participate in their teams’ calls by silently monitoring the call and barging into the call as needed.
  • When a call arrives from an anonymous or private number, Zendesk now creates a new user profile and ticket.
  • We've updated the phone icon label from Contact Center to Voice. This change represents the specific channel rather than a product name, and it is part of an ongoing effort to replace product names in the application with clearer navigation and labels.

Contact Center app

  • The Contact Center app can now be configured to run without Cognito. If you’re having issues related to authentication (missed calls, agent logout), submit a request to Zendesk Customer Support.
  • Removed customer profiles-related UI for customers who don’t use customer profiles.

Fixed:

Contact Center app

  • When a missed call is routed back to the same agent in Contact Center, the answer option is delayed, and the accept and decline controls remain on screen after the call is accepted, leaving the call UI in an inconsistent state until the application is refreshed.
  • If an agent missed an inbound call and was auto-set to Unavailable, switching back to Available could leave the call console in a broken state. This update restores normal call flow and console behavior so agents can continue handling calls without needing to refresh or logout and login.

Apps and integrations

New:

  • Updated the Zendesk Slack app layout with dedicated Chat and History tabs, accessible via the main app view or Slack's split-view side panel.

  • Active conversational chat features will be available exclusively for Employee Service (ES) accounts on July 30.

Mobile SDK's

Android

Breaking Change Notice: The next major version of the Android SDK will require a minimum API level of 24 (Android 7.0). This update is necessary to support the latest Compose BOM requirements.

New:

  • End users can now upload file attachments from within conversation extension web views using the native file picker.
  • End users can now download a transcript of their conversation directly from the conversation screen. See How to enable download transcripts.

Fixed:

  • Fixed an issue where the conversation header subtitle could briefly appear while the conversation was loading or being transferred to an agent or bot.
  • Fixed an issue where the typing indicator did not display the agent's name while they were typing.
  • Fixed an issue where shorthand color values (such as #fff or #000) from theme settings were not applied correctly and fell back to the default color.
  • Fixed a regression where calling the NewConversation API opened an existing conversation instead of creating a new one.
  • Updated the SDK to Kotlin 2.2.21 to support Kotlin versions 2.1 through 2.3. Compatibility for version 2.0.x is now deprecated. This update ensures compatibility for customer applications built on recent Kotlin releases.

iOS

New:

  • The SDK now requires a minimum deployment target of iOS 16. Make sure your app targets iOS 16 or later before updating.

Fixed:

  • Fixed an issue where deep links to older conversations could fail to open because the cache was validated too early.
  • Fixed an issue where a cached session was not cleared on expired-JWT logout when switching between users.
  • Fixed an issue where buttons containing no text were not visible.
  • Fixed a VoiceOver accessibility issue so the "New" messages divider is now correctly announced.
  • Fixed an issue so file label text now respects the device's accessibility text size settings.

App Marketplace

New:
  • Problem Portfolio (Support)
    • Problem Portfolio helps you manage problem tickets and their linked incidents from a single dashboard.  A navbar dashboard lists every active Problem with the count of linked Incidents, the age of the oldest Incident, and a severity score computed from impact. Filter by assignee, priority, tag, or any existing custom field — and group Problems by any dimension you choose. Drill into a Problem to see all linked Incidents. Multi-select and bulk-solve, bulk-tag, or bulk-reassign up to 100 Incidents at a time with rate-limit-aware chunking.
  • Access Monitor (Support) (paid)
    • Access Monitor helps you see who opens sensitive Zendesk tickets and logs it automatically.  Set rules on ticket tags, agent roles, or non-assignee views. When a rule matches, Access Monitor can do things like add a short private internal note to the ticket, apply a tag, log the view in a dedicated access monitor, track last viewer, last view time, and running view count, or add specified agents as ticket followers so they are notified.
  • Mello Claims (Support)
    • Mello is a freight audit and claims platform that helps shippers and logistics teams recover money lost to carrier errors. Mello automatically audits parcel and freight invoices for overcharges and streamlines the filing and tracking of damage, loss, and shortage claims across carriers — turning a slow, manual recovery process into an automated one. Mello Claims brings that recovery workflow directly into Zendesk Support. When a customer contacts your team about a damaged, lost, or delayed shipment, your agents can file a Mello claim without ever leaving the ticket.
  • Hide.fy (Support) (paid)
    • HIde.fy gives you instant, fine-grained control over what each agent sees in Zendesk. No code. No workarounds. Rules apply in real time, directly inside Zendesk Support. Hide.fy lets you define exactly what each agent, group, or brand sees — and everything else disappears. Automatically. Rules are built visually in a central dashboard and take effect immediately — no deploys, no configuration files, no developer required.
  • Skip.ly (Support) (paid)
    • Skip.ly turns Zendesk's skip log into a live, filterable analytics dashboard.  Get visibility into skip volume over time, who is skipping the most tickets, which skip reasons come up most, top tickets that get skipped, which customers are skipped the most, and more.
  • Enreach Omnichannel (Support)
    • Enreach Omnichannel lets you make and receive calls from Zendesk, automate ticket creation, and record call information. Easily integrate your phone system from the Zendesk control panel.
  • Luna (Theme)
    • Luna is a modern, fully responsive Zendesk Guide Help Center theme for teams that want a polished self-service experience without writing custom code. Built on Templating API v4, Luna covers the full Guide ecosystem—knowledge base, community, requests, approvals, generative answers, and service catalog—with a cohesive visual system and 80+ theme settings organized in a clear admin panel.
  • Monday.com by Git-Zen (Support) (paid)
    • Monday.com by Git-Zen lets you create Monday.com items from Zendesk and sync updates both ways.  Your operations and project work lives on monday.com boards. Your customer issues live in Zendesk. When those two worlds don't talk, teams duplicate effort, and customers wait longer than they should. Git-Zen connects them so Zendesk tickets flow directly into monday.com, and every board update is automatically visible in the ticket.
  • Trello by Git-Zen (Support) (paid)
    • Trello by Git-Zen lets you create Trello cards from Zendesk and sync updates both ways.  Your team tracks work on Trello boards. Customer issues come in through Zendesk. Right now, moving something from one to the other means copying and pasting, and then manually checking on progress. Git-Zen creates that connection automatically. Create cards from tickets, sync comments, and see every board update inside Zendesk.
  • Asana by Git-Zen (Support) (paid)
    • Asana by Git-Zen lets you create Asana tasks from Zendesk tickets and sync comments both ways. Support tickets that need cross-team action often fall through the cracks. An agent files a bug, a feature request goes in Slack, and nobody tracks whether anything actually happened. Git-Zen gives every Zendesk ticket a direct line into Asana. Create tasks, set assignees, and watch updates flow back automatically.
  • ClickUp by Git-Zen (Support) (paid)
    • ClickUp by Git-Zen lets you create ClickUp tasks from Zendesk tickets and sync comments both ways. Your roadmap lives in ClickUp. Customer issues live in Zendesk. Without a connection between them, support agents are guessing at status and product teams are missing customer context. Git-Zen links both tools so ticket escalations land directly in ClickUp, and every update flows back to Zendesk automatically.
  • Notion by Git-Zen (Support) (paid)
    • Notion by Git-Zen lets you create Notion pages from Zendesk tickets and sync comments both ways. Your team documents everything in Notion: product decisions, bug tracking, project work. Your customers submit issues in Zendesk. Git-Zen connects both, so support tickets can create and link directly to Notion pages, and updates flow back automatically.

Products with no updates this week

  • Support
  • AI agents - Advanced
  • Knowledge
  • AI agents
  • Analytics
  • Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM)
  • Zendesk QA

articles.name: Announcing new action builder connectors
articles.title: Announcing new action builder connectors
articles.body:
Zendesk is excited to introduce 10 new action builder connectors that help teams automate workflows across IT service management, CRM, ERP, HR, marketing, and analytics.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What's changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What's changing?

Zendesk is introducing ten new connectors for action builder, enabling teams to automate more workflows across the tools they use every day. Together, these connectors help organizations build end-to-end automation that spans departments, reduces manual work, and keeps information flowing between systems.

The new connectors include: 

  • ServiceNow enables incident and case management across platforms, allowing teams to create, update, and synchronize ITSM workflows between Zendesk and ServiceNow.
  • monday.com, Microsoft Planner, and Azure DevOps help support and engineering teams automatically create tasks, track issues, and keep project status synchronized without manual handoffs.
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales and Dynamics 365 Business Central bring CRM and ERP automation into Zendesk workflows, allowing teams to sync customer records, create invoices, and manage sales pipelines directly from tickets.
  • HiBob automates HR workflows such as onboarding, time-off tracking, and employee record management.
  • Iterable triggers personalized marketing campaigns and tracks customer engagement events based on support interactions.
  • New Relic enables technical operations and data teams to query observability data and create alerts, while Snowflake provides direct access to data warehouse queries and insights.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Organizations increasingly need to connect customer service operations with systems across IT service management, finance, engineering, HR, marketing, and data analytics. These new connectors address those needs by:

  • Unifying ITSM and service operations so incidents and cases stay updated.
  • Accelerating cross-functional workflows through automated task creation, status updates, and information sharing.
  • Reducing manual data entry and errors by syncing customer records, employee data, and business transactions.
  • Bringing observability metrics, analytics queries, and campaign engagement data into support workflows.
  • Improving employee service delivery through automated HR processes triggered by service requests.
  • Strengthening customer engagement through connected marketing automation and follow-up journeys.

By connecting these business platforms to action builder, teams can deliver faster, more accurate service using the tools they use every day.

What do I need to do?

These connectors are being rolled out to all accounts with access to action flows. For more information, see Understanding the action builder and action flows.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum, where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Using ServiceNow actions in action flows
articles.title: Using ServiceNow actions in action flows
articles.body:
Before you can include external actions in your action flows, you must connect the action builder to the external system.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

You can connect action flows to ServiceNow to automate creating, updating, searching, and looking up incidents, cases, and users. Use OAuth with a dedicated service account for secure integration. This connection lets you manage ITSM incidents and customer service cases directly within your workflows, improving collaboration and data accuracy across platforms.

By connecting the action builder to external systems, such as ServiceNow, admins can integrate Zendesk with external systems in automated workflows, improving collaboration and maintaining a seamless experience across multiple platforms.
Note: The steps associated with external systems in action flows are referred to collectively as external actions.
This article contains the following topics:
  • Connecting ServiceNow to action builder
  • Using ServiceNow actions in action flows

Connecting ServiceNow to action builder

Before you can include external actions in your action flows, you must connect the action builder to the external system.

When connecting to external systems for use in action flows, the following best practices are recommended:
  • All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it's a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.
  • All integrations request access to necessary scopes. However, it's important that you review and validate the scopes before authorizing the connection to the external system.
  • When managing credentials for API key-based tools, such as OpenAI, it's best to store keys in a secure vault or credential manager.

To set up OAuth in ServiceNow

Before connecting, you must register an OAuth application in ServiceNow.

The ServiceNow connection requires the useraccount OAuth scope, which enables read and write access to ServiceNow user accounts, incidents, cases, and related records. Review the scope carefully before authorizing the connection. This permission allows action flows to create and modify ServiceNow records on your behalf.

  1. Log into your ServiceNow instance as an admin.
  2. Navigate to System OAuth > Application Registry.
  3. Click New > Create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients.
  4. Enter a name for your application (for example, "Zendesk Action Flows").
  5. Set the Redirect URL to the value provided in the Zendesk connection dialog.
  6. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret values.
  7. Save the application registry entry.
To connect action builder to ServiceNow
  1. In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Actions > Action flows.
  2. Create or edit an action flow.
  3. Open the step sidebar.
  4. Under External actions, click ServiceNow.
  5. Click Connect.
  6. Enter your ServiceNow instance subdomain (for example, "dev12345" from dev12345.service-now.com).
  7. Enter your OAuth Client ID and OAuth Client Secret from your ServiceNow application registry.
  8. Follow ServiceNow's prompts to authenticate and complete the connection.
    Note: All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it is a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.

After you've connected to the system, you'll see an indicator that it's connected and details about the instance you're connected to, as well as the actions available for ServiceNow.

Using ServiceNow actions in action flows

The following ServiceNow actions are available:
  • Create incident
  • Update incident
  • Search incidents
  • Lookup incident
  • Create case
  • Update case
  • Search cases
  • Lookup case
  • Lookup user
  • Search users

Creating an incident

Use the Create incident action to create a new ITSM incident record in ServiceNow. This action dynamically loads all available fields (standard and custom) from your ServiceNow incident table at runtime.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Short Description, Caller

Optional: Dynamic fields loaded from your ServiceNow instance (standard and custom fields)
Output Incident details including sys_id, number, short description, state, priority, assignment information, timestamps, and activity status.

Updating an incident

Use the Update incident action to modify fields and status of an existing ServiceNow incident. This action dynamically loads all available incident fields from your ServiceNow instance.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Sys ID

Optional: Dynamic fields loaded from your ServiceNow instance (standard and custom fields)
Output Updated incident details including sys_id, number, description, state, priority, assignment information, resolution details, and timestamps.

Searching for incidents

Use the Search incidents action to find incidents matching specific filter criteria.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: Number, Short Description, State, Priority, Assignment Group, Assigned To, Caller, Category, Active, Opened At From, Opened At To, Created From, Created To, Limit, Offset, Query

All search filters are optional. Combine multiple filters to narrow results. Use Limit and Offset for pagination.
Output Array of incident objects containing sys_id, number, descriptions, state, priority, assignment details, dates, and activity information, plus total count and pagination flag.

Looking up an incident

Use the Lookup incident action to retrieve a single incident by sys_id or incident number.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: Sys ID, Incident Number, Display Value, Exclude Reference Link

You must provide Sys ID or Incident Number to look up an incident.

Use Display Value to control whether reference fields return sys_ids or display names.
Output Complete incident details including sys_id, number, descriptions, state, priority, urgency, impact, assignment information, caller details, resolution details, timestamps, and SLA information.

Creating a case

Use the Create case action to create a new customer service case in ServiceNow CSM. This action dynamically loads all available fields from your ServiceNow case table.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: If dynamic loading fails, this action requires Short Description, Account, Contact, and State as minimum fields.

Optional: Dynamic fields loaded from your ServiceNow case table.
Output Case details including sys_id, number, short description, state, priority, category, account and contact information, assignment details, and timestamps.

Updating a case

Use the Update case action to modify fields and status of an existing ServiceNow case. This action dynamically loads all available case fields from your ServiceNow instance.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Sys ID

Optional: Dynamic fields loaded from your ServiceNow case table (standard and custom fields)
Output Updated case details including sys_id, number, description, state, priority, assignment information, escalation status, and timestamps.

Searching for cases

Use the Search cases action to find customer service cases matching specific filter criteria.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: Multiple filter fields including case number, description, state, priority, account, contact, assignment details, dates, and pagination controls.

All search filters are optional. Combine multiple filters to narrow results. Use Limit and Offset for pagination.
Output Array of case objects containing sys_id, number, descriptions, state, priority, account and contact information, assignment details, and timestamps, plus total count and pagination flag.

Looking up a case

Use the Lookup case action to retrieve a single case by sys_id or case number.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: Sys ID, Case Number, Display Value, Exclude Reference Link (at least one of Sys ID or Case Number required)

You must provide either Sys ID or Case Number to lookup a case. Use Display Value to control whether reference fields return sys_ids or display names.
Output Complete case details including sys_id, number, descriptions, state, priority, account and contact information, assignment details, resolution information, and timestamps.

Looking up a user

Use the Lookup user action to retrieve a single ServiceNow user by sys_id or email address.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: Sys ID, Email, Display Value, Active (at least one of Sys ID or Case Number required)

You must provide either Sys ID or Email to look up a user. Use the Active filter to return only active users.
Output User details including sys_id, username, first and last name, full name, email, active status, job title, department, manager, phone numbers, timezone, and creation date

Searching for users

Use the Search users action to find ServiceNow users by name, email, username, or department.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs

Optional: Name, Email, Username, Active, Department, Limit, Offset

All search filters are optional and support partial matching (except Username which requires exact match). Use Limit and Offset for pagination.
Output Array of user objects containing sys_id, username, names, email, active status, job title, department, manager, contact information, and timezone, plus total count and pagination flag.

articles.name: Service Incident - July 16, 2026 - Chat | Pod 25 - Ticket creation delays
articles.title: Service Incident - July 16, 2026 - Chat | Pod 25 - Ticket creation delays
articles.body:
Summary

On July 16, 2026 from 03:50 UTC to 05:36 UTC , Chat (Agent Workspace) customers in Pod 25 experienced degraded performance, primarily elevated latency and delays when creating tickets. Messaging was not affected.
 

Timeline

July 16, 2026 5:23 UTC 
We are actively investigating an issue affecting customers in Pod 25, which is causing a degraded experience in Chat within Agent Workspace. Customers may experience delays when creating tickets. The Messaging product should not be affected. Our engineers are actively working to resolve the issue, and we will provide an update as soon as more information becomes available. Thank you for your patience.

July 16, 2026 5:56 UTC
The service has now recovered, and performance returned to normal levels at approximately 5:36 AM UTC. We are continuing to monitor closely for any recurrence and investigating the underlying contributors to help ensure stability and prevent a repeat. Thank you for your patience.
 
July 16, 2026 6:34 UTC 
We’re happy to share that the issue causing degraded Chat performance in Agent Workspace has been resolved, and service is now operating normally again. We’ve also put preventive measures in place to help reduce the likelihood of recurrence while we continue our follow-up investigation. Thank you again for your patience and understanding.
 

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a sudden surge of high-volume ticket update activity from a single customer account, which led to unexpected load on the database supporting Ticket Log Service in Pod 25. That database load resulted in processing delays that impacted Chat ticket creation in Agent Workspace.
 

Resolution

To fix this issue, we implemented a temporary rate limit on the high-volume traffic pattern to protect overall service stability. After the limit was put in place, database load reduced and service performance returned to normal.
 

Remediation Items

To reduce the likelihood of this happening again, we are taking steps including:

  1. Improving query-level monitoring and alerting so we can detect expensive database query patterns earlier
  2. Reducing unnecessary database work in Ticket Log Service that can amplify load during traffic spikes
  3. Reviewing safeguards (such as targeted throttling) to prevent a single customer’s automation from degrading performance for other customers on the same Pod
     

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Using Iterable actions in action flows
articles.title: Using Iterable actions in action flows
articles.body:
Before you can include external actions in your action flows, you must connect the action builder to the external system.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

You can connect action flows to Iterable using a server-side API key to automate user profile management, event tracking, comments, and email campaigns. Actions include creating, updating, and looking up users, sending triggered emails, and managing campaigns. Use a dedicated service account for integration and specify the correct data center to ensure proper authentication and smooth workflow automation across platforms.

By connecting the action builder to external systems, such as Iterable, admins can integrate Zendesk with external systems in automated workflows, improving collaboration and maintaining a seamless experience across multiple platforms.
Note: The steps associated with external systems in action flows are referred to collectively as external actions.
This article contains the following topics:
  • Connecting Iterable to action builder
  • Using Iterable actions in action flows

Connecting Iterable to action builder

Before you can include external actions in your action flows, you must connect the action builder to the external system.

When connecting to external systems for use in action flows, the following best practices are recommended:
  • All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it's a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.
  • All integrations request access to necessary scopes. However, it's important that you review and validate the scopes before authorizing the connection to the external system.
  • When managing credentials for API key-based tools, such as OpenAI, it's best to store keys in a secure vault or credential manager.

To create an API key

The Iterable connection requires a server-side API key from your Iterable project. Read-only API keys will not work. Ensure you create a server-side API key with appropriate write permissions.
  1. Log in to your Iterable account.
  2. Navigate to Integrations > API Keys.
  3. Create a new server-side API key.
  4. Save the key or keep the window open so you can copy and paste it into Zendesk.

    You'll need it when connecting Iterable to action builder.

To connect action builder to Iterable
  1. In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Actions > Action flows.
  2. Create or edit an action flow.
  3. Open the step sidebar.
  4. Under External actions, click Iterable.
  5. Click Connect.
  6. Follow Iterable's prompts to authenticate and complete the connection:
    • Enter your Iterable server-side API key.
    • Specify your data center region (US or EU). If your Iterable account is hosted in the European Union data center, you must specify "EU" as the data center. If left empty, the connection defaults to the US data center (api.iterable.com). Using the wrong data center will cause authentication failures.
    Note: All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it is a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.

After you've connected to the system, you'll see an indicator that it's connected and details about the instance you're connected to, as well as the actions available for Iterable.

Using Iterable actions in action flows

The following Iterable actions are available:
  • Create user
  • Update user
  • Lookup user
  • Create event
  • Add comment
  • Send email to user
  • Lookup campaign
  • List campaigns

Creating a user

Use the Create user action to create a new user profile in Iterable. If the user already exists, their profile will be updated with the provided information (upsert behavior).

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Email

Optional: User ID, Data fields, Prefer user ID, Create new fields, Merge nested objects
Output Success status, message, email, and user ID.

Updating a user

Use the Update user action to update an existing user profile in Iterable. If the user does not exist, a new profile will be created with the provided information (upsert behavior).

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Email

Optional: User ID, Data fields, Prefer user ID, Create new fields, Merge nested objects
Output Success status, message, email, and user ID.

Looking up a user

Use the Lookup user action to retrieve a user profile by email address or user ID.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Identifier type, Identifier value
Output User profile details including email, user ID, signup date, profile updated date, and custom data fields.

Creating an event

Use the Create event action to track a custom event for a user in Iterable. Events can be used for segmentation, campaign triggers, and analytics.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Email, Event name

Optional: User ID, Data fields, Event ID, Campaign, Template, Create new fields
Output Success status, message, event name, email, user ID, and event ID.

Adding a comment

Use the Add comment action to add a comment or note to a user profile. The comment is stored as a custom field in the user's data fields.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Email, Comment

Optional: User ID, Field name
Output Success status, message, email, user ID, and field name where comment was stored.

Sending an email to a user

Use the Send email to user action to send a triggered email to a user using an Iterable campaign. The campaign must be in a triggerable state.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Campaign, Recipient email

Optional: Data fields, Send at
Output Success status, message, campaign ID, recipient email, and scheduled send time.

Looking up a campaign

Use the Lookup campaign action to retrieve campaign details including name, status, type, and template information.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Campaign
Output Campaign details including ID, name, state, type, template ID, list IDs, send time, created date, and updated date.

Listing campaigns

Use the List campaigns action to retrieve all campaigns in your Iterable project.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs None
Output Array of campaign objects containing ID, name, state, and type, plus total count.

articles.name: Service Incident - July 14, 2026 - AI Agents | Multiple Pods - AI Agents Repeating Messages
articles.title: Service Incident - July 14, 2026 - AI Agents | Multiple Pods - AI Agents Repeating Messages
articles.body:
Summary

On July 14, 2026, between 14:40 UTC and 17:00 UTC, some customers experienced AI Agents getting stuck in loops and sending repeated messages in bot conversations. In some cases, this continued even after an end user stopped responding or after a human agent replied.
 

Timeline

July 14, 2026 17:21 UTC 
We are aware of an issue affecting bot conversations causing looped or repeating messages across multiple pods. Our team is investigating and we will provide further updates shortly.
 
July 14, 2026 17:37 UTC 
We have rolled back a recent change which appears to have caused messaging conversations to loop or repeat bot messages, and we are seeing conversation errors drop off. Please let us know if you are still experiencing any issues in conversations.
 
July 14, 2026 18:13 UTC 
We are happy to report that the issue causing repeated and looping messages in bot conversations has been resolved. Thank you for your patience during our investigation.
 

Root Cause Analysis

A change to a cleanup job increased query timeouts to accommodate a growing backlog. Under real production load, the query ran long enough to hold locks on key database tables, blocking the live webhook processing path.

This lock contention resulted in database “lock wait timeout” errors during inbound webhook processing, preventing conversation state from being updated and leading to repeated/looping bot behavior.
 

Resolution

  • We confirmed the issue via logs and reproduction in a test account.
  • We rolled back the cleanup job change.
  • After rollback, conversation processing errors dropped and customer reports indicated the looping/repeating behavior stopped.
     

Remediation Items

We are taking steps to reduce the likelihood of recurrence and improve earlier detection:

  • Query and job improvements: Rework and optimize the cleanup process so it can handle backlog safely without locking behavior that impacts live traffic.
  • Monitoring and alerting: Add/adjust monitoring so we detect job failures, rising lock-wait timeouts, and related error patterns earlier.
  • Operational safeguards: Review rollout safeguards for changes that can affect database performance or locking, especially for background jobs sharing the same database as live request paths.
     

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Using Microsoft Azure DevOps actions in action flows
articles.title: Using Microsoft Azure DevOps actions in action flows
articles.body:
Before you can include external actions in your action flows, you must connect the action builder to the external system.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

You can connect action builder to Microsoft Azure DevOps to automate workflows that create, update, and manage work items, pull requests, projects, and pipelines. Use external actions like creating work items, adding comments, triggering pipeline runs, and retrieving statuses to improve collaboration and streamline task management across platforms. Use a dedicated service account for secure authentication and proper permissions.

By connecting the action builder to external systems, such as Microsoft Azure DevOps, admins can integrate Zendesk with external systems in automated workflows, improving collaboration and maintaining a seamless experience across multiple platforms.
Note: The steps associated with external systems in action flows are referred to collectively as external actions.
This article contains the following topics:
  • Connecting Microsoft Azure DevOps to action builder
  • Using Microsoft Azure DevOps actions in action flows

Connecting Microsoft Azure DevOps to action builder

Before you can include external actions in your action flows, you must connect the action builder to the external system.

When connecting to external systems for use in action flows, the following best practices are recommended:
  • All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it's a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.
  • All integrations request access to necessary scopes. However, it's important that you review and validate the scopes before authorizing the connection to the external system.
  • When managing credentials for API key-based tools, such as OpenAI, it's best to store keys in a secure vault or credential manager.
To connect action builder to Microsoft Azure DevOps
  1. In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Actions > Action flows.
  2. Create or edit an action flow.
  3. Open the step sidebar.
  4. Under External actions, click Microsoft Azure DevOps.
  5. Click Connect.
  6. Follow Microsoft Azure DevOps's prompts to authenticate and complete the connection.

    The Microsoft Azure DevOps connection uses OAuth 2.0 for secure authentication. You'll be redirected to Microsoft to authorize access to your Azure DevOps organization. The connector automatically handles token refresh when needed.

    Ensure the authenticating user has appropriate permissions in your Azure DevOps organization for the operations you plan to perform through action flows.

    Note: All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it is a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.

After you've connected to the system, you'll see an indicator that it's connected and details about the instance you're connected to, as well as the actions available for Microsoft Azure DevOps.

Using Microsoft Azure DevOps actions in action flows

The following Microsoft Azure DevOps actions are available:
  • Create work item
  • Update work item
  • Lookup work item
  • Add comment to work item
  • List work items
  • Create pull request
  • Update pull request
  • Lookup pull request
  • List pull requests
  • Lookup project
  • List projects
  • List pipelines
  • Trigger pipeline run
  • Get pipeline status
  • List pipeline runs

Creating a work item

Use the Create work item action to create a new work item in an Azure DevOps project.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Work item type, Title

The Work item type field dynamically populates based on your project configuration and may include Bug, Task, User Story, Epic, Feature, or custom types.

Optional: Description, Assigned to, State, Priority, Tags, Area path, Iteration path, Repro steps, Acceptance criteria, Story points, Original estimate, Remaining work, Severity, Activity, Parent ID, Reason

Optional fields vary by work item type (for example, Repro steps for Bugs, Acceptance criteria for User Stories).
Output Work item object including id, rev, work_item_type, title, description, state, assigned_to, created_date, changed_date, url, and all field details.

Updating a work item

Use the Update work item action to modify an existing work item's fields.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Work item ID

Optional: Project, Title, Description, Assigned to, State, Priority, Tags, Reason, Area path, Iteration path, Remaining work, Completed work, Story points, Severity, Activity

Only provided fields are changed. Existing values for fields you don't specify remain unchanged.

Selecting a Project enables state, area path, and iteration path options specific to that project.
Output Updated work item object including id, rev, work_item_type, title, changed_date, url, and all updated field details.

Looking up a work item

Use the Lookup work item action to retrieve detailed information about a specific work item by its ID.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Work item ID

Optional: Expand relations, Expand comments

Set Expand relations to Yes to include parent, child, and related work items as well as links and attachments.

Set Expand comments to Yes to include all comments and discussion history.
Output Work item object including all fields, with optional parent, children, related_work_items, attachments, and comments array.

Adding a comment to a work item

Use the Add comment to work item action to post a comment on a work item.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Work item ID, Comment text
Output Comment object including comment_id, work_item_id, text, created_by, created_date, modified_date, url, and comment_version.

Listing work items

Use the List work items action to search for work items using WIQL (Work Item Query Language) or filter fields.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project

Optional: Query, Title contains, Work item type, State, Assigned to, Tags contain, Area path, Max results, Sort field, Sort order

You can use the Query field to write custom WIQL queries for advanced filtering, or leave it blank to use the simple filter fields below.

Max results defaults to 50 and cannot exceed 200.

Sort field accepts Changed Date, Created Date, Title, or Priority.
Output Results array of work items with total_count and has_more pagination flag.

Creating a pull request

Use the Create pull request action to create a new pull request in a Git repository.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Repository, Source branch, Target branch, Title

Optional: Description, Reviewers, Work item IDs, Is draft, Auto complete, Labels, Merge strategy, Delete source branch

Branch names should use the format feature/branch-name or refs/heads/feature/branch-name.

Reviewers should be comma-separated email addresses.

Work item IDs should be comma-separated numeric IDs.

Set Is draft to Yes to create as a draft pull request.
Output Pull request object including pull_request_id, title, description, status, created_date, created_by, repository, source_branch, target_branch, reviewers array, work_item_refs array, url, and web_url.

Updating a pull request

Use the Update pull request action to modify an existing pull request.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Repository, Pull request ID

Optional: Title, Description, Status, Is draft, Auto complete enabled, Merge strategy

Only provided fields are changed.

Status accepts active, completed, or abandoned.

Set Auto complete enabled to Yes to automatically merge when all policies pass.
Output Updated pull request object including pull_request_id, title, status, merge details, last_merge_commit, closed_date, url, and web_url.

Looking up a pull request

Use the Lookup pull request action to retrieve detailed information about a specific pull request.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Repository, Pull request ID

Optional: Include commits, Include work items

Set Include commits to Yes to retrieve all commits included in the pull request.

Set Include work items to Yes to retrieve linked work items.
Output Detailed pull request object including all fields, reviewers array, labels array, optional commits and work_item_refs arrays, completion_options, url, and web_url.

Listing pull requests

Use the List pull requests action to retrieve pull requests from a Git repository.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Repository

Optional: Status, Creator ID, Reviewer ID, Source branch, Target branch, Max results, Skip

Status accepts all (default), active, completed, or abandoned.

Max results accepts 1-100 (default: 50).

Use Skip for pagination to skip the first N results.
Output Pull requests array with pull request objects plus pagination details with total_count and has_more flag.

Looking up a project

Use the Lookup project action to retrieve details about a specific Azure DevOps project.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project

Optional: Include capabilities, Include history

Set Include capabilities to Yes to retrieve version control and process template details.

Set Include history to Yes to retrieve project change history.
Output Project object including id, name, description, state, visibility, default_team, url, with optional capabilities and history.

Listing projects

Use the List projects action to retrieve all projects in an organization.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization

Optional: State filter, Continuation token, Max results

State filter accepts All, WellFormed (active projects, default), Deleting, or New.

Max results accepts 1-100 (default: 100).
Output Projects array with project objects including id, name, description, state, visibility, and url, plus total_count and continuation_token.

Listing pipelines

Use the List pipelines action to retrieve build and release pipelines in a project.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project

Optional: Pipeline name, Folder path, Continuation token

Pipeline name supports partial matching. Folder path format is \Production or \CI\Builds.
Output Pipelines array with pipeline objects including id, name, folder, revision, url, and web_url, plus total_count and continuation_token.

Triggering a pipeline run

Use the Trigger pipeline run action to manually trigger a pipeline execution.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Pipeline ID

Optional: Branch, Variables, Resources repositories, Stages to skip

Branch format is main or refs/heads/feature/branch-name.

Variables should be a JSON object (for example, {"Environment": "Production"}).
Output Run object including run_id, run_number, pipeline details, state, result, created_date, finished_date, url, and web_url.

Getting pipeline run status

Use the Get pipeline run status action to retrieve the status and details of a pipeline run.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Pipeline ID, Run ID
Output Detailed run object including run_id, run_number, name, state, result, pipeline details, created_date, and finished_date.

State indicates the current status (in progress, completed, canceling, cancelled). Result indicates the outcome (succeeded, failed, canceled, etc.).

Listing pipeline runs

Use the List pipeline runs action to retrieve recent runs for a specific pipeline.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Pipeline ID

Optional: Result filter, State filter, Max results, Continuation token

Result filter accepts all, succeeded, failed, etc. Max results accepts 1-100 (default: 50).
Output Runs array with run objects including run_id, run_number, state, result, and urls, plus total_count and continuation_token.

articles.name: Do I need authorization from Zendesk to perform a penetration test?
articles.title: Do I need authorization from Zendesk to perform a penetration test?
articles.body:
Question

I would like to perform a penetration test. Do I need authorization from Zendesk?

Answer

No, you don't need authorization from Zendesk to perform a penetration test. You can perform this test anytime, but Zendesk recommends avoiding Thursdays. Zendesk usually runs deployments on Thursdays, which may cause scanners to report false positives or false negatives.

To do the test, you must abide by the terms of the responsible disclosure policy and follow the Bugcrowd guidelines:

  • No test likely to cause service outages for other tenants is tolerated, such as DoS, DDoS, or RDDoS
  • Social engineering Zendesk or sub-contractor activities aren't allowed

After you complete the test, submit your results to security@zendesk.com. The team identifies any issues.

Available actions let you execute SQL statements, find tables with pattern filters, and retrieve detailed table schema information, helping you manage data and automate tasks across platforms effectively.

Connecting Snowflake to action builder

Before you can include external actions in your action flows, you must connect the action builder to the external system.

When connecting to external systems for use in action flows, the following best practices are recommended:
  • All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it's a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.
  • All integrations request access to necessary scopes. However, it's important that you review and validate the scopes before authorizing the connection to the external system.
  • When managing credentials for API key-based tools, such as OpenAI, it's best to store keys in a secure vault or credential manager.

The Snowflake connection uses OAuth 2.0 authentication with the authorization code grant type. You will need to provide three pieces of information:

  • Account Identifier: Your Snowflake account identifier (for example, APAC_DEV.AWS_AP_NORTHEAST_1)

  • OAuth Client ID: OAuth client ID from your Snowflake security integration

  • OAuth Client Secret: OAuth client secret from your Snowflake security integration

To set up OAuth authentication in Snowflake

  1. Create a security integration in Snowflake with OAuth settings.
  2. Generate the client ID and client secret credentials.
  3. Configure the appropriate redirect URIs for action flows.
To connect action builder to Snowflake
  1. In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Actions > Action flows.
  2. Create or edit an action flow.
  3. Open the step sidebar.
  4. Under External actions, click Snowflake.
  5. Click Connect.
  6. Follow Snowflake's prompts to authenticate and complete the connection.

    The connector uses the refresh_token scope during authentication. Role and warehouse are specified per action at execution time, providing flexibility to choose appropriate resources based on workload needs.

    Review the requested permissions carefully before authorizing the connection. Keep your client secret secure and do not share it or commit it to version control.

    Note: All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it is a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.

After you've connected to the system, you'll see an indicator that it's connected and details about the instance you're connected to, as well as the actions available for Snowflake.

Using Snowflake actions in action flows

The following Snowflake actions are available:
  • Executing a query
  • Searching tables
  • Looking up a table schema

Executing a query

Use the Execute query action to run arbitrary SQL statements in Snowflake.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: SQL statement, Warehouse, Role

Optional: Timeout

Consider the following when using the Execute query action:
  • The SQL statement field supports all SQL statement types including SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, ALTER, and others.
  • The Warehouse field is a searchable dropdown of available warehouses.
  • The Role field is a searchable dropdown of available roles.
  • The Timeout field specifies query timeout in seconds.
  • For SELECT queries, the data array contains row data as key-value pairs.
  • For INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE operations, the rows affected field shows the number of rows modified.
Output Query execution results including statement handle, status URL, execution message, row count, rows affected, and data array for SELECT queries.

Searching tables

Use the Search tables action to discover tables in a Snowflake database schema with optional pattern filtering.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Database, Schema, Warehouse, Role

Optional: Table name pattern

Consider the following when using the Search tables action:
  • The Database field is a searchable dropdown of available databases.
  • The Schema field is a searchable dropdown that depends on the selected database.
  • The Table name pattern field accepts SQL LIKE patterns for filtering (for example, "USER%" to find tables starting with USER).
  • The Warehouse and Role fields are searchable dropdowns.
Output Array of table objects containing name, kind, row count, byte size, and creation date, along with total count.

The kind field indicates the table type (TABLE, VIEW, etc.).

Looking up a table schema

Use the Lookup table schema action to retrieve column definitions and metadata for a specific Snowflake table.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Database, Schema, Table, Warehouse, Role
Consider the following when using the Lookup table schema action:
  • The Database field is a searchable dropdown of available databases.
  • The Schema field is a searchable dropdown that depends on the selected database.
  • The Table field is a searchable dropdown that depends on both database and schema selections.
  • The Warehouse and Role fields are searchable dropdowns.
Output Array of column objects containing name, data type, nullable status, default value, and primary key indicator, along with array of primary key column names.

The column output includes data type information (for example, VARCHAR, NUMBER, DATE), whether each column accepts null values, default values if defined, and whether the column is part of the primary key. The primary keys field provides a separate list of all primary key column names for convenience.

Summary: ◀▼

You can connect action flows to Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central to automate workflows involving customers, sales invoices, vendors, and purchase invoices. Use actions like lookup, search, create, and update for these records. Connecting requires OAuth 2.0 authentication with a service account having proper permissions. This integration helps manage external system data directly within your workflows, improving collaboration and data accuracy.

By connecting the action builder to external systems, such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, admins can integrate Zendesk with external systems in automated workflows, improving collaboration and maintaining a seamless experience across multiple platforms.
Note: The steps associated with external systems in action flows are referred to collectively as external actions.
This article contains the following topics:
  • Connecting Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central to action builder
  • Using Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central actions in action flows

Connecting Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central to action builder

Before you can include external actions in your action flows, you must connect the action builder to the external system.

When connecting to external systems for use in action flows, the following best practices are recommended:
  • All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it's a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.
  • All integrations request access to necessary scopes. However, it's important that you review and validate the scopes before authorizing the connection to the external system.
  • When managing credentials for API key-based tools, such as OpenAI, it's best to store keys in a secure vault or credential manager.
The Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central connection uses OAuth 2.0 authentication with the following required configuration:
  • Azure Tenant ID: Your Azure Active Directory Tenant ID in GUID format.

    You can find your Azure tenant ID under Azure Active Directory > Properties.

  • Company ID: Your Business Central company ID in GUID format.

    You can find your Company ID by navigating to your company settings or by examining the URL when logged in to Business Central.

  • Environment: Optional environment name (production or sandbox). Defaults to production if not specified.
Important: Ensure the service account has appropriate permissions in Business Central to perform the actions you intend to use in your workflows. The account should have read/write access to customers, sales invoices, vendors, and purchase invoices as needed.
To connect action builder to Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central
  1. In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Actions > Action flows.
  2. Create or edit an action flow.
  3. Open the step sidebar.
  4. Under External actions, click Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.
  5. Click Connect.
  6. Follow Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central's prompts to authenticate and authorize the connection.
    Note: All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it is a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.

articles.name: Release notes through 2026-07-17
articles.title: Release notes through 2026-07-17
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of what was released last month.

This week's release notes include:

  • Voice
  • Knowledge
  • Copilot
  • AI agents
  • App Marketplace
  • Products with no updates this week

Voice

New:

  •  Agents can now change the incoming call ringtone and adjust the incoming call volume.  For more information. See Receiving incoming calls.

Fixed:

  • When an agent makes an outbound call and the end user declines or blocks the call, the agent will now see an error message informing them the call was declined or busy. Previously, the call would end without any indication or error message.    

Knowledge

New:

  • Contentful is now available as a knowledge source. You can connect Contentful to your Zendesk account to make the content available wherever external content is used.
  • Jira is now available as a knowledge source. You can connect Jira to your Zendesk account to make the content available wherever external content is used.
  • We’ve released an Early Access Program (EAP) for the conversational help center experience, delivered through the new Lisbon theme. This EAP introduces an AI-powered help center layout that combines natural-language question answering with standard help center navigation, allowing end users to ask questions and receive quick answers generated from your published content.

Fixed: 

Web Crawler

  • Crawler run reports now correctly classify empty title and empty body validation errors instead of showing them as "Undetermined" errors.
  • Crawler CSV reports now include error descriptions even when the background worker is terminated due to memory limits.
  • Crawlers now correctly handle all successful HTTP response codes (201-299), not just 200.
  • Removed per-URL ping validation from start URL input to support large-scale crawlers with up to 1500 URLs.

Help Center

  • Fixed product navigation links on custom domains. Admins using custom Help Center domains (for example, help.yourcompany.com) can now correctly navigate to other Zendesk products like Workforce Management from the product navigation tray. Previously, these links pointed to the custom domain instead of the native Zendesk subdomain, causing navigation failures.
  • Updated the "Get help" menu link. The agent navbar's "Get help" menu now points to the correct Knowledge Help Center section instead of the deprecated Support Help Center URL.

Copilot

New:

  • Auto assist can now generate suggestions based on content from external sources and internal knowledge articles. This allows you to broaden the pool of content available to auto assist so it can provide suggestions on even more topics and tickets. See Connecting external knowledge sources to your Zendesk account and Setting up a web crawler.
  • We’re updating the auto assist composer experience in the Agent Workspace to make AI suggestions feel like a natural part of replying to customers - without interrupting an agent’s workflow. Beginning on June 22, we’ll start rolling out this update to accounts over a period of two weeks. See Using auto assist to solve tickets.
  • Auto assist can now use similar solved tickets as a knowledge source across all channels and languages when no procedures or articles are available. This gives agents more relevant reply suggestions based on how customer issues are being resolved in real time, helping teams respond faster and deliver more consistent support. See About auto assist.

AI agents

New:

AI Copilot Procedure Management

  • In the procedure insights side panel, the recommendations section now appears below the insights section for a more logical reading order
  • Article sources in procedure improvement recommendation cards now link directly to the Help Center article instead of the editor. You can review the source content without navigating away from your workflow.
  • When Admin Copilot saves a procedure as a draft, the confirmation message now includes two links - one to open the procedure in the editor and one to return to the full procedures list.

Fixed:

AI Copilot Procedure Management

  • Procedure editor URL no longer carries over pagination state: opening a procedure from a paginated list previously added cursor and pagination query parameters to the editor URL. Those are now dropped on navigation.
  • New procedure recommendations no longer disappear when a malformed ID is present. A single malformed procedure ID in a batch request was causing all new procedure recommendations to be silently dropped for affected accounts. 

App Marketplace

New:
  • FastPass IVM (Support)
    • FastPass IVM is the leading provider of secure identity verification solutions. The FastPass Identity Verification Manager (IVM) for Zendesk brings forced, contextual identity verification directly into the support agent's workflow, ensuring every password reset and sensitive request is handled securely and in compliance with enterprise policy. With this integration, agents no longer need to switch between systems. When a ticket is opened, the app automatically checks ticket status, tags, and requester details against your configured eligibility rules — and either presents a one-click Launch button or automatically opens the FastPass IVM Client. This protects your service desk against social engineering and vishing attacks when they are most likely to occur.
  • ServeTech Skill Tracer (Support) (paid)
    • ServeTech Skill Tracer analyzes your team's real ticket history in Zendesk to identify how each agent performs across ticket categories. It uses a transparent, statistics-based scoring model to surface true specializations and then creates and maintains skill tags in Zendesk automatically — no manual work required. ServeTech works from your existing ticket categories — no custom taxonomy to define, no agents to manually tag. Install it, and your existing Zendesk skills-based routing starts working.
  • ScriptRunner (Support)
    • ScriptRunner helps Zendesk teams automate operational workflows, run secure scripts, and build lightweight internal tools directly inside Zendesk. Use ScriptRunner to handle repetitive admin tasks, validate ticket data, enrich support workflows, and give agents and admins purpose-built tools without switching systems or building a separate Zendesk app for every process.
  • Okta Workflows (Support)
    • Okta Workflows empowers organizations to automate complex identity processes and user lifecycle management without writing code. By integrating Okta Workflows with Zendesk, IT and support teams can seamlessly orchestrate actions based on real-time events. With this integration, you can build custom identity workflows that connect Zendesk to your broader tech stack. Automatically create or update Zendesk user profiles when changes occur in Okta, freeze accounts during offboarding events, or trigger multi-system alerts when high-priority access requests are made.
  • OneClick (Support) (paid)
    • OneClick turns your most common ticket actions into sidebar buttons. Agents update status, assignment, tags, and custom fields in one click—instead of opening multiple fields on every ticket. Save a preset once; apply it to any ticket with a single click. Build buttons in the nav bar app, or share one list account-wide for every agent. Choose who can manage buttons and optionally deploy a shared list via app settings.
  • EVOX (Support)
    • EVOX builds cloud-based call center solutions trusted by customer service teams. This integration connects your EVOX phone system directly to Zendesk Support. Every inbound and outbound call is automatically matched to the right customer and ticket — no manual lookups, no missed records. Instantly identify callers by phone number and open the relevant ticket, automatically create a new ticket and end-user profile when no match is found, and log full call detail records (CDRs) to Zendesk Custom Objects for reporting and compliance.
  • Escalation Guard (Support) (paid)
    • Escalation Guard helps agents submit cleaner, more complete escalations from the Zendesk ticket sidebar. Agents choose an escalation type, complete the required fields, and submit a formatted internal note. Escalation Guard applies routing tags so admins can use Zendesk triggers, views, and automations to route work to the right team.
  • ResolveReady (Support) (paid)
    • ResolveReady helps stop agents from resolving tickets with missing data, skipped steps, or incomplete approvals. ResolveReady enforces ticket completeness before agents can resolve. Admins can build solve-readiness workflows without code. Workflows trigger by ticket tag, form, group, brand, status, or field value. Agents see required steps in the ticket sidebar and complete them once, and each completed item saves directly to a mapped Zendesk ticket field or internal note.
  • VeriDraft (Support)
    • VeriDraft connects to Zendesk and turns any customer message into a ready-to-send reply written entirely from your Terms of Service, SOPs, and compliance documents. Every claim is backed by a real citation, every answer shows how confident it is, and when VeriDraft can't find a grounded answer, it says so — instead of making one up.

Products with no updates this week

  • Admin Center
  • Support
  • AI agents - Advanced
  • Analytics
  • Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM)
  • Zendesk QA

articles.name: Announcing step-level error handling and search in action builder
articles.title: Announcing step-level error handling and search in action builder
articles.body:
Zendesk is excited to announce several enhancements to action builders and custom actions that give you more visibility, flexibility, and scale when building action flows.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

The following improvements are now available for action flows and custom actions:

  • Error handling for each step: You can now decide what happens when a step fails. You can choose to halt the flow or continue execution, and configure specific paths for success or failure.
  •  Search triggers and actions easily: You can now perform keyword searches for triggers and actions when setting up your workflows.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Together, these updates unlock a set of highly requested customer use cases and make action flows even more powerful in automating work across the Zendesk ecosystem:

  • This release provides Zendesk customers with the ability to configure error handling behavior on each step of their workflows. Users can choose to create separate execution paths for the success and failure of a step, or configure the "continue on error" option so that flows do not halt unexpectedly. This ensures customers are instantly aware of any failures within a flow so they can be proactively handled.
  • Additionally, customers will now have an easy way to search for triggers and actions, removing the friction of trying to locate specific actions manually. In short, this release makes action builder more capable, flexible, and better equipped to support advanced workflow automation.

What do I need to do?

These enhancements are being rolled out to all accounts with access to action builders. No action is required on your part to activate them.

To get started, see Understanding the action builder and action flows and Creating action flows to automate processes.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Service Incident -  July 9, 2026 - Forethought | Solve widget load failures and elevated API errors
articles.title: Service Incident -  July 9, 2026 - Forethought | Solve widget load failures and elevated API errors
articles.body:
Summary

On July 9, 2026, some customers experienced issues loading the Forethought Solve widget and saw elevated errors when the widget attempted to communicate with our backend services. The issue was caused by a software change that increased backend workload and led to timeouts.
 

Timeline

July 09, 2026 17:34 UTC
We are currently investigating an issue where the Solve Widget is failing to load for some customers. Our engineering team has identified a potential cause and is in the process of rolling back suspected changes to restore service.
 
July 09, 2026 17:41 UTC 
The suspected changes have been successfully rolled back. We are currently seeing traffic recovering and the Solve Widget is beginning to load successfully for affected customers.
 
July 09, 2026 17:58 UTC 
This incident has been fully resolved. The Solve Widget is now loading normally for all customers, and our monitoring confirms that performance and traffic have returned to stable levels following the rollback.
 

Customer impact

Between 16:59 UTC and 17:31 UTC on July 9, 2026, customers using the Solve widget across several pods experienced one or more of the following:
  • The Solve widget failed to open or load
  • The Solve widget displayed frequent error messages
  • Requests to our Solve API returned elevated errors
  • Some customers also experienced degraded access to related dashboards and analytics
During this window, customers could not reliably use the widget.
 

Root Cause Analysis

A recently released change introduced a bug in a synchronization flow used by the widget. Under certain conditions, the widget and backend services retried and repeated work more than intended.
This led to:
  • A spike in “cache misses” (the system could not reuse previously prepared data)
  • Increased fallback to slower backend data retrieval
  • Saturation of backend capacity, causing request queues to build and requests to time out
These effects reinforced each other (retries created more load), resulting in elevated errors and widget load failures.
 

Resolution

We restored service by:
  • Rolling back the problematic release
  • Reducing background load that was competing for the same backend capacity
  • Scaling up the Solve API service to clear backlogs and stabilize performance
After these mitigations, error rates returned to near zero and response times returned to normal.
 

Remediation Items

We’re making changes to prevent similar issues, including:
  • Adding automated tests and safeguards for “non-existent conversation” scenarios
  • Ensuring the widget does not continue polling/retrying in situations where it should stop
  • Adding additional validation before performing expensive backend retrieval work
  • Improving monitoring to detect early signals of this type of overload more quickly
     

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

Can I transfer my phone number to use it with Zendesk Voice (formerly Talk) or Zendesk Sales?

Answer

Yes, you can port your number into either Voice (formerly Talk) or Sales if you have a paid subscription. You can't port numbers on Talk trial accounts.

Prerequisites

Question

Can I use an email alias, distribution list, shared mailbox, or Google Group as a support address?

Answer

Zendesk does not support the use of aliases, distribution lists, shared mailboxes, Google Groups, or non-standard email clients or services. These configurations add routing complexities and cause issues with troubleshooting. However, many companies successfully set up and maintain these configurations without issue. Zendesk does not block their use.

To connect these configurations, see To add an external support address in Zendesk.

While aliases, distribution lists, shared mailboxes, and Google Groups are common, they can introduce unique challenges and complications:

  • Complex routing and troubleshooting. Adding another layer of processing increases deliverability risks due to spam filters or lost emails.
  • Malformation of email headers. Relays can alter email headers, which causes Sender Policy Framework (SPF), DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM), or Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC) issues.
  • Fickle nature of email processing. Email behavior can vary based on the processor and parameters, which highlights the need for a direct and simple pathway.
Note: Zendesk highly recommends the use of standard email addresses for maximum deliverability. Unsupported configurations like these can cause issues that an admin cannot troubleshoot. If you use these options, Zendesk cannot help with any problems that arise.

To connect to a Google Group, see How do I use Google Groups as a support address?
